pages.title: A Plan for a Greener Europe
pages.content:
The European Commission announced the Green Deal on 11 December 2019. The Green Deal is a plan to help the economy grow in a sustainable way. Its aim is to protect the planet by building a clean economy. By 2050, the European Union (EU) wants to reduce its net greenhouse gas emissions to zero. The Green Deal shows how the EU can make its economy, industry, and everyday life more eco-friendly. In this way, it wants to fight climate change and keep the planet healthy.

One important goal is to manage materials, water, and energy more carefully. The Green Deal supports a circular economy. In a circular economy, people recycle materials and produce less waste, so nature is protected. To reach this goal, the Green Deal offers a big plan with useful rules and new opportunities.

vocabulary.definition: Able to continue for a long time without harming the environment.
The system of money, work, and business in a country.
A gas, such as carbon dioxide, that keeps heat in the air and makes the Earth warmer.
Gases that cars, factories, and power stations send into the air.
Not harmful to the environment.
An economy in which people repair, reuse, and recycle things instead of throwing them away.

pages.title: The Main Aims
pages.content:
The main aims of the Green Deal are these:

Fighting Climate Change: Climate change is one of the EU’s most important problems. The EU and its member countries want to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030. They also want to reach climate neutrality by 2050. This is an important step. It can limit global warming and reduce the bad effects of climate change.

Protecting Nature: The Green Deal wants people to benefit from nature responsibly. It wants to stop problems like deforestation, using too much water, and losing biodiversity. It also wants to protect and repair the environment. The goal is clean air, clean water, healthy land, and healthy food for everyone.

A New Economy: The Green Deal supports green technologies and businesses that are kind to the environment. In this way, the economy can grow without hurting nature.

vocabulary.definition: The slow rise in the temperature of the Earth.
A situation in which a country does not add more greenhouse gases to the air than it removes from it.
Cutting down the trees of a forest over a large area.

pages.title: Why Is the Green Deal Important?
pages.content:
The Green Deal is important because climate change and environmental damage are a serious danger to the planet. Old ways of doing business use too much water, land, and energy, and they burn too many fossil fuels. We cannot continue like this for long. For this reason, many people see a net-zero economy as the key way to fight climate change, protect biodiversity, and have safe energy in the future.

Today, safe energy is a big problem. Wars and problems between countries make the future difficult to predict. High energy prices and broken supply chains have negatively affected many companies, especially industries that consume a lot of energy. Wars can block trade routes and stop deliveries. As a result, electricity and fuel become hard to find and expensive.

vocabulary.definition: Fuels such as coal, oil, and gas that formed under the ground millions of years ago.
When the greenhouse gases that we send into the air are equal to the amount that we take out of it.
All the companies and steps that bring a product from the factory to the customer.

pages.title: Moving to Renewable Energy
pages.content:
Because of this, more and more countries are moving to renewable energy, such as wind and solar power. Renewable energy is often cheaper, and it helps countries quit depending on expensive fossil fuels. To keep industry strong in these difficult times, countries need new rules, more renewable energy, and workers with new skills.

For this reason, the transition to a green economy must speed up, so that industries can get clean energy at a fair price. Governments and organizations should make a complete plan. This plan should show how much money is needed for new clean technology and factories.

vocabulary.definition: Electricity that we make from the light of the sun.

pages.title: New Opportunities in a Net-Zero Age
pages.content:
In the next 20 or 30 years, a net-zero age will begin. In this age, the greenhouse gases that we send into the air will be equal to the amount that we take out of it. This new economy will bring new markets, new clean technologies, and a completely different energy system. Countries that put money into clean technology early and move fast can secure a strong position in this new economy. They can also become world leaders in clean technology and in the fight against climate change and pollution.

The move to a green economy creates new industries. These industries need workers with new skills. Factories also become more modern and more eco-friendly. To support this, the EU made a law called the Net-Zero Industry Act. It helps Europe build important green technologies, such as batteries, wind turbines, heat pumps, solar panels, and systems that catch and store carbon dioxide.

vocabulary.definition: A flat piece of equipment that makes electricity from the light of the sun.
A gas that comes out when we burn coal, oil, or gas.
A tall machine that makes electricity from the wind.
A machine that moves heat from the air or the ground to warm or cool a building.

pages.title: New Rules for Green Products
pages.content: New rules for eco-friendly products and clean energy are also important. These rules help people build, reuse, and recycle green technologies around the world. For example, large companies in the EU are no longer allowed to destroy clothes that they could not sell. Other rules make spare parts easy to find, so people can repair their things. In the future, these rules will cover many more everyday products. Factories will need to follow strict rules to preserve nature. Governments will see net-zero technologies as essential.

pages.title: Smart Choices and Green Jobs
pages.content:
In fact, the success of the Green Deal depends a lot on people. Consumers need to make smart, eco-friendly choices, and for this they need clear information. Before they buy a product, people should easily see how green, durable, and clean it is. Clear information helps people choose green products instead of products that cause a lot of pollution. For example, energy labels on fridges and washing machines help people compare products easily. Giving consumers more information is an important step toward a green economy.

This change in the economy is also changing the job market. As part of this change, the number of green jobs has grown fast in recent years. Workers at all levels need new skills, so large-scale training programs are necessary. Clean energy companies and eco-friendly factories still need more workers. As a result, companies will compete hard for workers with the right skills in the near future.

languageFocusExercises.explanation: “A depends on B” means B is necessary for A, or B decides what happens to A.

pages.title: Education and Working Together
pages.content:
In conclusion, the success of the green change will depend mostly on how well countries train workers and teach people. This is true for competitive industry, for a fair change that protects everyone, and for net-zero goals. For this reason, education is a big part of the Green Deal. It helps everyone learn important green and digital skills. Education and training are necessary for the shared future of the world.

Leaders, organizations, and ordinary people should all support these steps and turn these ideas into real actions for a cleaner world. Climate change does not stop at borders, so it is helpful for countries to keep working together with their international partners. Türkiye also published its own Green Deal Action Plan in 2021, and its goal is to reach net-zero emissions by 2053.

exercises.question: By how much does the EU want to reduce emissions by 2030?
exercises.fillBlanksText: The EU and its member countries want to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least [blank]% by 2030.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: “… reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 55% by 2030.”

feedback.correct: Correct. 55.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first aim in Chapter 2.

exercises.title: Industry and Energy
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: Which industries have high energy prices affected most?
options: industries that consume a lot of energy
exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “… especially industries that consume a lot of energy.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Energy-hungry industries.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Causes and Results
exercises.instructions: Match each cause with its result.
exercises.question: What happens as a result?

matchingPairs.left: Spare parts are easy to find.
Climate change does not stop at borders.

exercises.explanation: These causes and results appear in Chapters 3, 6, 7 and 8.

feedback.correct: Correct. Each cause matches its result.
feedback.incorrect: Look for so and as a result.

exercises.title: The Plan
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: The complete plan should show how much money is needed for new clean technology and factories.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “This plan should show how much money is needed for new clean technology and factories.”

feedback.correct: Correct. It should show the costs.

exercises.title: Success
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: The book says the success of the Green Deal does not depend on ordinary people.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “In fact, the success of the Green Deal depends a lot on people.”

feedback.correct: Correct. It depends a lot on people.

exercises.title: Skills
exercises.instructions: Complete the sentence from Chapter 8 with one word.
exercises.question: What does education help everyone learn?
exercises.fillBlanksText: It helps everyone learn important green and [blank] skills.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 8: “It helps everyone learn important green and digital skills.”

feedback.correct: Correct. Digital.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 8.

exercises.title: Leaders of the Future
exercises.instructions: Choose the answer that the book supports.
exercises.question: What can early investors in clean technology become?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “They can also become world leaders in clean technology and in the fight against climate change and pollution.”

feedback.correct: Correct. World leaders in clean technology.
feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Put the Dates in Order
exercises.instructions: Put the events in order.
exercises.question: What comes first, next and last?

sequencingItems.text: The European Commission announces the Green Deal (2019).
Türkiye publishes its Green Deal Action Plan (2021).
The EU wants emissions at least 55% lower (2030).
The EU wants to reach climate neutrality (2050).
Türkiye wants to reach net-zero emissions (2053).

exercises.explanation: The dates come from Chapters 1, 2 and 8.

feedback.correct: Correct. From 2019 to 2053.
